mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a growing economy, leading to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate exceeds 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong economy with growing demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts increase and unemployment rate decreases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a growing supply of goods and services, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate decreases and money supply increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment increases above 135000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index and an increase in housing starts indicate a strong economy with growing demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the consumer price index decreases and housing starts increase (t-test p > 0.05).
